cases.prompt: Help me design a Python Google ADK support assistant on Google Cloud before we write code. It should answer policy questions and eventually change customer bookings. Talk through the product requirements with me, challenge the architecture choices, and capture a design we can implement later.
cases.rationale: An early system design conversation spans product requirements, authority boundaries and architecture decisions before implementation.

cases.prompt: Review our proposed ADK system architecture with me. A browser sends a tenant ID to an agent on Cloud Run, all tenants share a document index, and the agent retries booking changes after a timeout. Help us revise the design and define how to validate its failure cases; do not implement it yet.
cases.rationale: A system-level architecture review needs connected decisions about identity, retrieval, external effects and failure validation.

cases.prompt: Our ADK assistant already has an accepted architecture and a profile store. Implement an explicitly saved response-language preference with a forget action and local tests. Keep the existing design and deployment setup.
cases.rationale: A focused implementation under an accepted architecture belongs to the memory specialist and should not restart a system design interview.

cases.prompt: Deploy this existing ADK service to the approved Cloud Run target using the reviewed configuration. Run the rollout checks and report the service endpoint; the architecture decisions are already settled.
cases.rationale: Executing an approved deployment belongs to the deployment specialist rather than pre-implementation system design.

cases.prompt: Help me design a conventional Django inventory application on Google Cloud. It needs a web interface, a database and scheduled stock imports. There are no agents or Google ADK components.
cases.rationale: Google Cloud hosting alone does not make generic application architecture an ADK system-design task.

cases.prompt: Our Python Google ADK assistant needs to remember a customer's preferred language and show its responses in our web app. Inspect the project, work out which parts need changing, and implement the feature with local tests.
cases.rationale: An outcome spanning memory and browser integration needs the entry point to select the relevant specialists.

cases.prompt: Change the loading spinner's color in our React app. The app happens to call an ADK backend, but leave the request handling and backend unchanged.
cases.rationale: An isolated styling change does not require ADK engineering guidance.

cases.prompt: Our ADK agent fetches two independent reports, then summarizes both. Run the fetches concurrently and make sure a failed branch cannot turn into a successful summary. Preserve the existing result schema.
cases.rationale: This changes parallel orchestration, handoffs and the workflow's failure contract.

cases.prompt: Our existing ADK agent already has the right execution flow. Add retrieval over the approved policy documents, including filtering documents by the caller's entitlement. Keep its orchestration unchanged.
cases.rationale: Governed document retrieval belongs to memory architecture; the request excludes control-flow changes.

cases.prompt: The refund API sometimes times out after accepting a request, and our Python agent retries it as a new refund. Fix the adapter so it preserves the same authorized operation and reports uncertain outcomes honestly.
cases.rationale: Ambiguous external writes and unsafe replay are the core API safety boundary.

cases.prompt: Our local SQLite report query is slow. Review its query plan and suggest an index; there is no HTTP client or external API involved.
cases.rationale: Ordinary query optimization has no external-call retry, deadline or replay problem.

cases.prompt: Our ADK assistant keeps repeating a tool that returns a terminal failure. Stop the repetition before another tool execution and enforce a model-call allowance across the whole invocation.
cases.rationale: The requested controls bound agent-level work and repeated tool dispatch.

cases.prompt: Add a timeout and bounded retries for transient errors to this one Python HTTP GET helper. Its caller already bounds agent invocations; leave those controls alone.
cases.rationale: A single HTTP retry policy belongs to API safety, not invocation-level guardrails.

cases.prompt: Prepare our existing Python ADK service for Cloud Run. Review the container entrypoint, runtime identity and session persistence, then produce the configuration and validation commands. Deployment is not authorized yet.
cases.rationale: Local preparation and review of ADK hosting are deployment work even without permission to execute cloud changes.

cases.prompt: Our ADK agent is already hosted successfully. Design how it should remember a user's explicitly saved language preference across conversations; no hosting or deployment changes are needed.
cases.rationale: Memory design alone is explicitly outside the deployment skill's activation scope.

cases.prompt: Traces show our ADK service on Cloud Run spends most of each request repeatedly creating its session client. Inspect that lifetime, reduce the measured overhead, and check that user isolation and cancellation still work.
cases.rationale: A measured session-handling bottleneck calls for optimization with correctness checks.

cases.prompt: We have a new ADK agent and need to choose between Cloud Run and managed Agent Runtime for its first deployment. Compare the hosting fit and prepare a deployment plan; we have no performance problem to investigate.
cases.rationale: Hosting selection and first deployment alone belong to the deployment specialist.

cases.prompt: Connect our existing ADK agent to a CopilotKit interface. Stream public text and tool progress, verify that the caller owns the conversation, and handle failures after a partial answer.
cases.rationale: The request concerns the browser transport, ownership and streamed-result contract.

cases.prompt: Make the message bubbles in our ADK chat page use a larger border radius and fix their mobile spacing. Keep the API, streaming and session behavior unchanged.
cases.rationale: Pure React styling does not need the agent-to-browser integration skill.

cases.prompt: Add a response-language preference to our ADK assistant. Save it only when the user explicitly agrees, keep it across restarts, isolate users, and let each user change or forget their own setting.
cases.rationale: An exact cross-session profile setting needs trusted scope, consent, persistence and erasure decisions.

cases.prompt: Tune the database server's buffer cache for our unrelated inventory application. This is database administration, with no agent sessions, retrieval or cross-session memory feature.
cases.rationale: General database administration and non-agent caching are excluded.

cases.prompt: Our ADK evaluation command reports success even when some cases have no score. Audit the result handling and add checks for missing cases, failed observations and the expected metric thresholds.
cases.rationale: Evaluation coverage, incomplete evidence and result auditing are the requested outcome.

cases.prompt: Add unit tests for this standalone Python date-formatting helper. It has no model, tools, runner or agent behavior to evaluate.
cases.rationale: Ordinary non-agent unit tests are outside the specialist's scope.

cases.prompt: Our ADK service must keep customer email addresses out of model requests, saved events and telemetry. Trace those paths, add the required screening boundaries, and use synthetic canaries to test them locally.
cases.rationale: The task requires sensitive-data controls across model, storage and export boundaries.

cases.prompt: Configure Cloud Armor rate limiting for a public marketing website. There is no ADK application, prompt screening or personal-data processing change in this task.
cases.rationale: Cloud Armor WAF configuration is distinct from agent sensitive-data protection and Model Armor.

cases.prompt: An ADK tool can select another customer's OAuth connection by passing their user ID. Move credential selection behind verified caller identity and test refresh and disconnect ownership.
cases.rationale: Model-controlled credential selection and delegated-token lifecycle need the tool-authentication specialist.

cases.prompt: Redesign our sign-in page's typography and password-field visibility button. Authentication already works; do not change identity verification, OAuth, credentials or agent tools.
cases.rationale: A sign-in UI change does not alter the tool authentication or credential boundary.

cases.prompt: Our ADK assistant's decisions on the labelled development cases are often wrong. Work out which kinds of error dominate, improve the prompt and exemplars, and re-measure. Keep the holdout untouched.
cases.rationale: Wrong decisions, error analysis and prompt or exemplar design are the evaluation skill's quality-iteration branch.

cases.prompt: Before our ADK agent reads this planning document pack, work out which pages are scans, tables or drawings and route them to OCR or a vision pass. Produce a per-page ingestion report.
cases.rationale: Document ingestion qualification before retrieval belongs to the memory and retrieval specialist.

cases.prompt: Rewrite the drafting prompt so the agent's decisions cite policies more consistently. Retrieval and storage already work; change the prompt and exemplars only.
cases.rationale: Prompt-only editing for decision quality is the evaluation skill's quality-iteration work, not memory architecture.

cases.prompt: Our drafting stage sometimes imposes a condition that its own reason says is waived, and it floods the officer with repeated warnings. Add in-code consistency checks and warning triage to the workflow.
cases.rationale: Consistency checks between stage outputs and warning triage are workflow contract repairs.

cases.prompt: I have four hours to build an ADK assistant that drafts decisions over a document pack, judged on five unseen cases and a report. Help me decide what to build first and what to leave out.
cases.rationale: Scoping a time-boxed, quality-judged build is the designer's scope gate and proportionality rule.

cases.prompt: Three of us have two weeks to ship an MVP of an ADK booking assistant, and we want to keep improving it afterwards. Plan what goes into the MVP, what waits, and how it fits the time we have.
cases.rationale: Fitting a design to a team's capacity and phasing MVP and later work is the designer's scope gate and delivery profiles.

cases.prompt: Build an ADK analytics assistant that answers revenue questions using reviewed query templates. Retrieve only the relevant schema and keep tenant scope and read-only query execution under application control.
cases.rationale: Natural-language analytics, selective schema context and controlled SQL execution define this specialist's task.

cases.prompt: Review indexes for a slow hand-written reporting query in our backend. No natural-language interface or agent-generated SQL is involved.
cases.rationale: Ordinary SQL tuning is explicitly excluded from the SQL-agent skill.

cases.prompt: Our ADK coordinator keeps sending refund questions to the billing agent instead of the refunds agent, and its 1,800-word instruction is full of MUST and NEVER rules nobody can review. Fix the sub-agent descriptions and restructure the root instruction, with a test that renders it against fixture state.
cases.rationale: Routing descriptions, instruction structure and a rendered-instruction test are the instruction specialist's work.

cases.prompt: Add a {customer_tier} placeholder and a JSON output example to this ADK agent's instruction without breaking state templating on google-adk 2.8.0, and explain which placeholders may be absent.
cases.rationale: Session-state templating, literal braces and optional placeholders are ADK instruction mechanics.

cases.prompt: Our agent's answers are wrong on 30% of the labelled development set. Run the error analysis by category, change one thing per iteration and report the holdout result.
cases.rationale: The measured decision-quality loop belongs to the evaluation specialist; no instruction mechanics or routing change is requested.

cases.prompt: Our ADK agent keeps calling search_orders when it should call get_order, and sometimes passes the customer name where the order ID goes. Review the tool docstrings and parameters and fix the declarations the model sees.
cases.rationale: Wrong tool selection and wrong parameters are model-facing interface defects in the tool declarations.

cases.prompt: We are adding a 40-tool MCP server to our ADK agent. Decide which tools to expose, how to name and filter them, and keep tool results from flooding the context.
cases.rationale: Tool-count budgeting, filtering, naming and result shaping are tool interface design decisions.

cases.prompt: The payments API times out and our refund tool sometimes charges twice when it retries. Fix the retry and idempotency behaviour.
cases.rationale: Retries, deadlines and duplicate writes of the external call belong to safe-api-tool-calls, not to the model-facing interface.

cases.prompt: Our ADK extraction agent returns fenced JSON and sometimes plain prose instead of the Pydantic output_schema, and it also has two tools. Make the structured output reliable without breaking tool use and show how to prove which path the model took.
cases.rationale: Output-schema validation, fences, the schema-with-tools path and repair loops are output-contract work.

cases.prompt: Everything runs on gemini-2.5-pro with temperature 0.2 and thinking_budget 2048. Move the right agents to a current Flash model, set thinking per agent and add a fallback for 429 errors, with a way to verify each change.
cases.rationale: Model selection, thinking and temperature configuration and failover are model-contract decisions.

cases.prompt: Add retries with backoff and an idempotency key to the payments tool that times out.
cases.rationale: An external-call retry policy involves no model configuration or output schema; safe-api-tool-calls owns it.

cases.prompt: Our ADK support agent gets slower and more expensive every turn after about thirty messages, cached token counts stay at zero and BigQuery tool results are 200 KB JSON blobs. Shape what enters each model request and verify the saving.
cases.rationale: Context-window growth, cache misses and oversized tool results are the optimise skill's context-window mode.

cases.prompt: Our ADK support agent reads customer emails and can issue refunds and send emails. Do a security review before launch and tell me what an attacker could make it do through a poisoned email or tool result.
cases.rationale: Untrusted content plus consequential actions is a whole-agent threat-model question, not a data-redaction task.

cases.prompt: We are adding three third-party MCP servers to the agent. How should we vet, filter and pin their tools, and what tests prove a poisoned tool description cannot make the agent leak data?
cases.rationale: MCP supply-chain vetting and adversarial assertions are security engineering.

cases.prompt: Customer social security numbers are showing up in our Cloud Logging entries from the agent. Add redaction before anything is logged.
cases.rationale: A sensitive-data class leaking into logs belongs to protect-adk-sensitive-data; there is no whole-agent threat or adversarial question.

cases.prompt: p95 latency on our Agent Runtime agent doubled this week. Add tracing and metrics so we can tell model time from tool time from session loading, and set an alert on it.
cases.rationale: Instrumenting signals, choosing the exporter for the host and alerting are production observability work.

cases.prompt: Pull the thumbs-down conversations from our BigQuery Agent Analytics table into an ADK eval set we can use for regression, with the personal data removed.
cases.rationale: Turning sampled production events into redacted evaluation cases is the production-to-evaluation hand-off.

cases.prompt: Set up Cloud Logging sinks and a 30-day retention policy for our GKE cluster's system logs.
cases.rationale: General logging administration with no agent telemetry, SLI or trace question.

cases.prompt: Google emailed that our Gemini model is retiring next month. Plan the upgrade so our agent's eval scores do not silently drop, including the judge model we use in CI.
cases.rationale: Model migration with re-baselining and judge pinning is release lifecycle work.

cases.prompt: Add an eval gate to GitHub Actions so pull requests that change the agent instruction are blocked on regressions, and make it not flaky or expensive.
cases.rationale: CI gate tiers, thresholds, repeats and cost ceilings are release engineering, not eval-case design.

cases.prompt: Deploy my ADK agent to Cloud Run for the first time with a service account and a session database.
cases.rationale: A first deployment belongs to deploy-adk-on-google-cloud; no versioning, gate or promotion concern is raised.

cases.prompt: Connect our ADK agent to the company's GitHub and Postgres MCP servers on Cloud Run, exposing only read tools, with per-user tokens that refresh and a check that the servers' tool lists have not changed since we reviewed them.
cases.rationale: Consuming MCP servers with filters, per-user headers and a pinned tool inventory is interoperability work.

cases.prompt: The billing team runs their agent in Java. Our ADK agent should delegate refund questions to it. Should we use A2A or just call their API, and what does the agent card and failure handling need to look like?
cases.rationale: The topology decision across a team and language boundary and the A2A contract are the interoperability specialist's modes.

cases.prompt: Split our pipeline into a writer and a reviewer sub-agent with a bounded revision loop and pass the draft through session state.
cases.rationale: In-process sub-agent orchestration with no process, team or protocol boundary belongs to adk-workflow-design.

cases.prompt: Our company sells advertising to small businesses and leadership wants to 'use AI' to sell more easily, but nobody has said where. Help me work out where in the buying journey AI would pay off, which workflow to improve first, and what business outcome we would measure, before anyone designs anything.
cases.rationale: The use case is not chosen yet; finding the friction, ranking opportunities and naming the outcome measure is discovery, which precedes system design.

cases.prompt: I run operations for a regional logistics firm. I keep hearing about AI agents but do not know how the technology works or which of our processes it could help. Ask me about the business and its numbers, then tell me where AI, ordinary automation or something else would make a difference and what to try first.
cases.rationale: A KPI-to-process discovery with a technology-fit judgement (agent, classical ML, rules or process change) is the skill's second entry mode.

cases.prompt: We have already decided to build an ADK assistant that recommends display campaigns and takes advertisers through checkout; the outcome metric is checkout completion. Design the architecture and the implementation plan for it.
cases.rationale: The use case and its measure are chosen; what remains is system design, so the designer leads and discovery should not reopen the choice.

cases.prompt: Write a market-sizing report on the advertising technology industry in Australia with competitor profiles and growth forecasts for our investor update.
cases.rationale: General market research for investors is not a search for where AI fits in the company's own processes.

cases.prompt: Our four-week ADK proof of concept is finished and the evidence is recorded in docs/plans/campaign-assistant.md. Prepare the presentation for the leadership review that decides whether we fund the production build: slide outline, what I say, and the questions they will ask. Then a separate technical version for the platform team.
cases.rationale: Turning recorded plan evidence into a stage-specific deck, narrative and question preparation for business and technical audiences is the presenter's job.

cases.prompt: The agent has been in production for three months with measured results in our plan. Draft a public case study we could share with our Google Cloud account team, with the approvals and numbers we need to gather first.
cases.rationale: A public case study built from recorded results, with its approval checklist, is the presenter's case-study mode.

cases.prompt: Add a demo mode to our ADK agent's React frontend so the sales team can show streamed replies on stage without a login.
cases.rationale: Changing the application for a demo is frontend implementation, not preparing a stakeholder presentation from evidence.

cases.prompt: Our evaluation report says every case passed but I suspect some tool failures were ignored. Audit the result files and tell me what the real pass rate is.
cases.rationale: Auditing evaluation results produces the evidence; presenting it to stakeholders is a later step and a different skill.

cases.prompt: Our ADK shopping agent's tools render product cards and a comparison chart next to the reply, but the cards show up twice and a refresh after a preference change never reaches the browser. Fix the widget pipeline.
cases.rationale: Interface widgets rendered by tools are an agent-to-browser contract the frontend specialist owns, including the staging and emission rules behind duplicate or vanishing widgets.

cases.prompt: Add an endpoint so users can list and delete the documents they uploaded to our ADK assistant.
cases.rationale: Owner-filtered domain routes behind the verified principal are ordinary backend work around the agent, which this skill owns.

cases.prompt: Set up migrations for our app tables; the ADK agent already stores sessions in the same Postgres.
cases.rationale: Application migrations must exclude ADK's session tables, a backend data boundary this skill owns.

cases.prompt: Generate a typed TypeScript client for the React app from the FastAPI backend of our ADK assistant and keep it in sync.
cases.rationale: The public OpenAPI contract, offline dump and drift-checked generated client belong to this skill.

cases.prompt: Stream tool progress into the chat UI while the ADK agent runs.
cases.rationale: The agent's run and stream contract and tool progress display belong to adk-frontend-integration.

cases.prompt: Each user should connect their own Google Drive for the ADK agent's tool.
cases.rationale: Delegated per-user OAuth for a tool belongs to adk-tool-auth-and-secrets.

cases.prompt: Build a FastAPI CRUD service for our inventory system.
cases.rationale: FastAPI work with no ADK agent is outside this toolkit; FastAPI's own skill covers it.

cases.prompt: Set up the look of our new ADK assistant's web app: a design system for the shadcn components, and how the chat shows running tools, an approval before filing a ticket, and an error that arrives after part of the answer.
cases.rationale: Setting up an ADK interface's design system and its agent UI states (tool timeline, approval prompt, failed turn) is now in this skill's scope; an isolated styling tweak stays out.

cases.prompt: We're four tickets into the support assistant build. Checkpoint docs/plans/support.md: one ticket changed what forgetting a preference means and we're running over the hours.
cases.rationale: Folding ticket evidence (a contract change, an overrun) back into the design and plan is the designer's checkpoint mode.

cases.prompt: Carry out the next ready ticket in docs/tickets/support/.
cases.rationale: Executing a ticket belongs to adk-engineer; the designer is only brought back when the ticket's evidence needs a decision.

cases.prompt: I build ADK proofs of concept for three clients and keep retyping each client's region, approval rules and who signs off. Set up something outside the repos so the discovery and design skills already know Acme's defaults next time, and bind this repo to Acme.
cases.rationale: Carrying the engineer's client context across projects, outside the repository, with a repository-to-org binding, is the practice profile's init and bind. In Codex the package disallows implicit invocation, so there it needs $practice-profile.

cases.prompt: Add memory to my ADK agent so it remembers each customer's preferences between sessions.
cases.rationale: Cross-session memory inside an ADK agent belongs to adk-memory-architecture; the practice profile is the engineer's own context, not the agent's.

cases.prompt: Add a rule to my ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md that I always want British spelling in every project.
cases.rationale: A host-wide preference for every project is an ordinary edit of the host's global instruction file; the practice profile holds per-org context read at specific steps.

cases.prompt: Import our strategy and AI policy Markdown files from docs/client/ into my client profile for Acme, so I don't have to type it all in again for the next project.
cases.rationale: Bringing company documents the user names into the engineer's cross-project org profile, confirmed line by line, is the practice profile's import action. In Codex it needs $practice-profile.

cases.prompt: Load these policy documents into my agent's knowledge base so it can answer staff questions about them.
cases.rationale: Retrieval over documents inside an ADK agent belongs to adk-memory-architecture; the practice profile holds the engineer's own org context.

cases.prompt: Summarise this strategy document for me in five bullet points.
cases.rationale: A one-off summary needs no skill; nothing is carried across projects or written to a profile.

cases.prompt: We need our underwriters to label about a hundred of the claims agent's answers so we have a gold set and can trust an LLM judge. How should we run the session, and how do we check whether the two underwriters agree?
cases.rationale: Planning a subject-matter-expert labelling session, inter-rater agreement and judge calibration on their labels is the expert-review mode of this skill.

cases.prompt: Set up an annotation project in Label Studio for our image classifier's training data, with three annotators per image.
cases.rationale: Training-data annotation for a non-agent image model is not ADK agent evaluation.

cases.prompt: The claims agent has been live since August. Write this month's one-page value report for our sponsor from the plan's measurement and incident records, and say whether we should stop, continue or scale.
cases.rationale: The monthly post-launch value report with a stop, continue or scale call is the presenter's value-report stage.

cases.prompt: Build a Looker Studio dashboard of the agent's daily token spend and latency from our BigQuery traces.
cases.rationale: A telemetry dashboard is observability work (adk-agent-observability), not a sponsor report built from recorded measurements.

cases.prompt: Draft the statement of work for the client from our discovery brief, design and plan; our rate is £95 an hour.
cases.rationale: Turning the design and plan into a statement of work, with deliverables mapped to goals and hours from the schedule check, is the designer's engagement scoping.

cases.prompt: The client now wants a second channel. Write the change request against our signed SOW and say which goals and estimates change.
cases.rationale: A change request cites the contracts, goals and estimates it changes from an updated plan; engagement scoping owns it.

cases.prompt: Negotiate our agency's standard master services agreement and payment terms with procurement.
cases.rationale: General contract negotiation with no ADK design or plan behind it is outside the toolkit; the SOW reference lists AI terms for counsel, it does not negotiate.

cases.prompt: We go live with the claims assistant in two weeks. Prepare the rollout pack: user guide, training, messages for managers and staff, and how we measure adoption.
cases.rationale: The go-live rollout pack written from the design's contracts and the plan's evidence is the presenter's rollout mode.

cases.prompt: Add an AI disclosure banner and a report-a-problem button to the chat UI of our ADK agent.
cases.rationale: Implementing interface components belongs to adk-frontend-integration (and the feedback endpoint to adk-agent-observability); the presenter writes the disclosure text, not the UI.

cases.prompt: Hand over our ADK agent to the client's IT team: support tiers, who owns which alert, moving IAM and secrets to them, and a postmortem template for agent incidents.
cases.rationale: Operations handover and the blameless agent postmortem extend the incident note this skill owns.

cases.prompt: Move our ADK agent's Cloud Run service into the client's GCP project and redeploy it there.
cases.rationale: Redeploying into another project is deployment work for deploy-adk-on-google-cloud; the handover decides who owns what, not how it is redeployed.

cases.prompt: Our client's DPO and legal team want the EU AI Act classification and the DPIA inputs for the CV-screening agent we designed before they approve the pilot. Draft them from docs/architecture/cv-screening.md and the plan's evidence.
cases.rationale: Drafting the AI Act classification and DPIA inputs from the design and plan evidence for a client's reviewers is this skill's deliverable.

cases.prompt: The client's CISO sent a vendor security questionnaire and asked for a system card for our ADK policy assistant. Answer it from what the design and plan actually record, and say what is only planned.
cases.rationale: A security-questionnaire answer bank and system card drawn from the design's contracts, security baseline and evidence belong to the governance pack.

cases.prompt: Redact PII from our agent's logs before they reach Cloud Logging.
cases.rationale: Implementing a sensitive-data control in the agent is protect-adk-sensitive-data's work; the governance pack only cites such controls.

cases.prompt: Threat-model our ADK agent that reads customer emails and can issue refunds, and add an adversarial test suite before the security review.
cases.rationale: Threat modelling and adversarial tests are adk-agent-security; the governance pack drafts reviewers' papers from their results.

cases.prompt: Add a gate to CI so a prompt or model change cannot be released if the evaluation score drops.
cases.rationale: Release gates belong to adk-release-engineering, even though governance reviewers may later ask about them.

cases.prompt: We built an internal HR assistant for an Australian retailer. It reads staff leave and roster records from Workday and runs on Gemini in Sydney. Their Privacy Officer wants to know what the Privacy Act needs from us before the pilot; draft the papers from our design and plan.
cases.rationale: Drafting a privacy impact assessment and regulatory screen for an Australian client from the design and plan is this skill's deliverable, even though no EU law is involved.

cases.prompt: Our Sydney team built a customer-service chatbot for a UK bank that also has EU customers, and we will support it from Australia. Their DPOs want the DPIA inputs and whatever covers our access to the data from here.
cases.rationale: UK and EU DPIA inputs and the transfer facts for an Australian consultancy's access are governance papers this skill drafts from the project record.

cases.prompt: A California logistics client wants to use our ADK resume screener in California and New York City. Their general counsel asked what US law requires before the pilot; draft the papers from the design and the backtest results.
cases.rationale: A US regulatory screen, risk assessment inputs and bias evidence for an automated hiring tool, drawn from the design and evaluation records, belong to the governance pack.

cases.prompt: Write the privacy policy page for our company website explaining how we use cookies and analytics.
cases.rationale: A general website privacy policy is not a governance paper about an ADK agent drawn from its design and evidence, even though it mentions privacy law.

cases.prompt: We built a public-facing service chatbot for a NSW agency on ADK and Gemini. Their Accountable Official wants the AIAF answers and whatever their privacy and legal teams need before the pilot; draft them from our design and plan.
cases.rationale: Draft answers for the NSW AIAF from the crosswalk, plus the NSW privacy, records and contract screen for a state agency client, are governance papers this skill drafts from the project record.

cases.prompt: A Commonwealth department wants to use our ADK claims-triage agent. Their assessing officer asked for our input to the DTA AI impact assessment and the transparency statement; prepare it from our docs.
cases.rationale: Inputs to the DTA AI impact assessment tool and transparency statement, drawn from the design and evidence for the agency's officers, are this skill's government form answers.

cases.prompt: Our customer-service agent for a retailer with stores in Auckland and Singapore goes to pilot next month. Their privacy officer and DPO want the privacy papers, including what covers our support access from Sydney.
cases.rationale: A New Zealand and Singapore privacy screen, with the transfer facts for an Australian consultancy's access, is a governance pack drawn from the project record.

cases.prompt: Draft the governance papers for our HR assistant before the pilot: the client employs staff in Quebec and Ontario, and their counsel asked whether Law 25 applies to the agent's leave decisions.
cases.rationale: Screening Quebec's private sector Act, its automated-decision and outside-Quebec rules and Ontario employment rules for an HR agent, with the question left to counsel, is this skill's deliverable.

cases.prompt: Redact PII from our agent's logs before they reach Cloud Logging.
cases.rationale: Keeping personal data out of logs is a sensitive-data boundary this skill implements; the word privacy does not make it a governance paper.

cases.prompt: Our CTO worries we'll be locked into Google. Using docs/architecture/claims.md and docs/plans/claims.md, write up what moving to AWS or Azure, or to LangGraph, would involve, without changing the GCP build.
cases.rationale: A separate assessment of what a move to another cloud or agent framework would involve for an accepted GCP and ADK design, leaving the build unchanged, is this skill's deliverable.

cases.prompt: Carry out docs/tickets/claims/G07.md from docs/plans/claims.md: the portability goal whose primary skill is adk-portability-planning.
cases.rationale: A portability goal's ticket names this skill and asks for docs/portability/<topic>.md, not code.

cases.prompt: A stakeholder asked which components of our existing ADK design on GCP are provider-specific and which replacement boundaries are worth keeping. Answer from docs/architecture/support.md without redesigning anything.
cases.rationale: Classifying an existing design's components by provider dependency and naming the boundaries worth having is the core of the portability assessment.

cases.prompt: Deploy our ADK agent to Cloud Run.
cases.rationale: Deploying on Google Cloud is deploy-adk-on-google-cloud; nothing here asks about lock-in or another provider.

cases.prompt: Add a fallback from Gemini to Claude when Gemini returns 429.
cases.rationale: Configuring model failover in the running agent is adk-model-and-output-contracts; the portability planner only assesses model portability in a document.

cases.prompt: Rewrite our ADK agent in LangGraph and deploy it on AWS.
cases.rationale: Building or migrating the application on another framework and cloud is a migration build, which this skill excludes; it only writes the assessment.

cases.prompt: Connect our agent to a remote A2A agent running on Azure.
cases.rationale: Wiring a remote A2A peer is adk-agent-interoperability, even though the peer runs on another cloud.

cases.prompt: Design a new ADK app on GCP for our claims team.
cases.rationale: A new design is adk-system-designer's work; the designer asks the lock-in question and only a yes adds a portability goal.

cases.prompt: In the FastAPI app around our ADK agent, GET /api/claims/{claim_id} returns another user's claim if you guess the ID. Fix the route and the shared principal dependency so every claims query filters by the signed-in owner, with tests.
cases.rationale: Owner filters in domain-route queries and the verified-principal dependency are the backend's (ownership map: another user's records through an HTTP route).

cases.prompt: Our ADK web app's /api/invoices list route returns every customer's invoices to any signed-in user. Add the owner filter to the query and a test; the agent's tools are not involved.
cases.rationale: A cross-user leak in an HTTP route with no tool hop belongs to adk-fastapi-backend, not tool authentication.

cases.prompt: Our ADK agent's lookup_invoices tool takes customer_id as a model argument, so a user asked the chat for another customer's invoices and got them. Make the tool act only for the verified caller.
cases.rationale: Identity at the tool hop (principal from trusted state, never a model argument) is adk-tool-auth-and-secrets.

cases.prompt: The ADK agent behind our FastAPI app has a get_orders tool whose user_id comes from the model's arguments, so a crafted message reads someone else's orders. Bind the tool to the verified caller.
cases.rationale: The leak is through an agent tool, which adk-tool-auth-and-secrets owns even though the app is FastAPI.

cases.prompt: In our ADK web app the chat sidebar lists other people's conversations and lets you resume them, because the sessions and run_sse endpoints trust the user_id the browser sends. Fix listing and continuation so only the owner's sessions work.
cases.rationale: The agent's run, stream and session endpoints are the agent-to-browser contract that adk-frontend-integration owns.

cases.prompt: Anyone can resume another user's ADK chat by posting their session_id to our /run_sse endpoint. Make continuation reject sessions the caller does not own and show an error state in the chat.
cases.rationale: Session continuation on the agent's stream endpoint is adk-frontend-integration, not a domain route.

cases.prompt: Before our ADK agent's issue_refund tool runs on amounts over $500, a finance reviewer must approve it. The request can wait hours and must survive a restart. Implement the approval hold and the reviewer's decision.
cases.rationale: Which actions wait for a human, the durable review record and the resume flow are adk-operational-guardrails.

cases.prompt: Add a step where a manager approves any refund over $500 before the agent's refund tool executes; decisions may come the next day.
cases.rationale: Deciding that a refund waits for human approval, and holding it, is adk-operational-guardrails; safe-api owns the write once approved.

cases.prompt: After a reviewer approved a refund, our ADK agent's call to the payment provider timed out and the retry refunded the customer twice. Make the approved refund run exactly once and report uncertain outcomes.
cases.rationale: Idempotent replay of an approved external write is safe-api-tool-calls.

cases.prompt: A payment was approved by a human, then the provider call timed out and our retry created a second payment. Fix the retry so the same approved payment cannot be submitted twice.
cases.rationale: The approval already happened; a duplicate write on retry is safe-api-tool-calls.

cases.prompt: Our ADK agent reads inbound supplier emails and can pay invoices and email customers. Which of its tools should require confirmation, and what could a poisoned email make it do?
cases.rationale: Tiering tools by danger from a threat model is adk-agent-security.

cases.prompt: Our agent reads untrusted web pages and has tools that send email and move money. Work out which tools an injected page could abuse and which ones need a human in the loop.
cases.rationale: Deciding which tools are dangerous from untrusted input is the security threat model, not approval mechanics.

cases.prompt: Wire ADK's require_confirmation on our transfer_funds tool so the run pauses for a human, persists the pending request, and resumes after approval or rejection.
cases.rationale: The confirmation-and-resume mechanics are adk-operational-guardrails.

cases.prompt: When our ADK agent's tool is waiting for confirmation, show an approve/reject card in the CopilotKit chat and keep the tool timeline correct after a rejection.
cases.rationale: Rendering the approval state in the browser is adk-frontend-integration.

cases.prompt: Design the approve and reject buttons that appear in our chat UI when the agent asks to file a ticket, and how the timeline looks after someone rejects.
cases.rationale: This is the approval UI, which adk-frontend-integration owns; the approval policy is unchanged.

cases.prompt: Our ADK chat sessions run to 200 turns and every request resends the whole history, so latency and token cost climb each turn. Add history trimming or a summariser without breaking function-call pairs, and measure the saving.
cases.rationale: What each model request carries within a session, measured on latency and tokens, is optimise-adk-on-google-cloud.

cases.prompt: Long ADK sessions get slow because each turn sends the full conversation history to the model. Cut what is sent per turn and show latency before and after.
cases.rationale: In-session history trimming for latency belongs to optimise-adk-on-google-cloud, not memory architecture.

cases.prompt: Our travel assistant should remember a user's preferred airline and recent trips when they come back next week in a new chat, scoped to that user, and forget them on request.
cases.rationale: What persists and is recalled across sessions, with scoping and erasure, is adk-memory-architecture.

cases.prompt: Our ADK agent forgets everything when a user starts a new chat session. Make it recall relevant past conversations, scoped per user, with a way to delete them.
cases.rationale: Cross-session recall is memory architecture; there is no measured performance problem.

cases.prompt: Add a GitHub Actions step that runs our existing ADK eval set on every pull request, repeats flaky cases three times, caps the judge spend and fails the build below 90%.
cases.rationale: Wiring an existing eval set into CI with thresholds, repeats and cost policy is adk-release-engineering.

cases.prompt: Write twenty evaluation cases for our ADK refund agent covering partial refunds, policy exceptions and ambiguous requests, with graders and a judge rubric we can trust.
cases.rationale: Writing cases and graders is adk-agent-evaluation.

cases.prompt: Our ADK agent's eval set is too small to catch regressions. Design new cases for the refund policy edge cases and a rubric for the LLM judge.
cases.rationale: Designing cases and a judge rubric is adk-agent-evaluation; release owns the gate that runs them.

cases.prompt: Our ADK triage agent's instruction has three few-shot examples that all approve, and it now approves too often. Rework the exemplars: how many, which labels, what order, and keep them as data with IDs.
cases.rationale: Exemplar choice, count, order and storage are adk-agent-instructions.

cases.prompt: Rewrite the few-shot examples in our ADK classifier's prompt so they are balanced across labels and use the same format as the required output.
cases.rationale: Editing exemplars is prompt design owned by adk-agent-instructions; nothing is being measured.

cases.prompt: We changed the few-shot exemplars in our ADK agent's prompt. Measure on our 40-case labelled development set whether decisions improved, with error categories before and after, and keep the holdout untouched.
cases.rationale: Measuring a prompt change on a labelled set is adk-agent-evaluation's quality iteration.

cases.prompt: Compare our agent's development-set score with the old and the new few-shot exemplars, categorise the remaining errors and report which version wins.
cases.rationale: The measured comparison belongs to adk-agent-evaluation; the wording is not changing.

cases.prompt: Our released ADK agent's Gemini model retires next quarter. Plan the migration: re-baseline the eval suite on the replacement, pin the new model ID in the release manifest and keep rollback ready.
cases.rationale: Executing a model migration in a release is adk-release-engineering.

cases.prompt: Which Gemini model and thinking level should our new ADK extraction agent use, given its strict JSON output contract and a tight latency budget?
cases.rationale: Choosing a model and its settings is adk-model-and-output-contracts; there is no release in question.

cases.prompt: Let our analysts ask the ADK agent questions like 'revenue by region last quarter' that turn into reviewed, read-only BigQuery queries.
cases.rationale: Natural-language analytics over BigQuery is adk-sql-agent-engineering.

cases.prompt: Our ADK assistant should recall a returning user's past orders, stored in BigQuery, scoped to that user and honouring erasure requests.
cases.rationale: A user's scoped history read for continuity is adk-memory-architecture, not a SQL agent.

cases.prompt: Our client's DPO wants a DPIA input pack and a records-of-processing entry for the ADK claims agent before the pilot decision.
cases.rationale: Privacy-impact papers are adk-governance-pack; no control is being built.

cases.prompt: Connect our ADK agent to the approved GitHub MCP server over streamable HTTP with a tool filter and a name prefix, and close the connection cleanly on shutdown.
cases.rationale: Wiring an already-approved MCP server is adk-agent-interoperability.

cases.prompt: When Gemini returns 429 errors, fall back to a second model for our ADK agent and record which model answered each turn.
cases.rationale: Model failover is adk-model-and-output-contracts, not an external API retry.

cases.prompt: Our ADK agent sometimes calls search_flights forty times with the same arguments in one turn. Stop the repetition and cap model calls per invocation.
cases.rationale: Stopping repeated calls and capping invocations is adk-operational-guardrails; the tool choice is not wrong.

cases.prompt: Stop our ADK agent spending more than $20 per user per day: refuse new turns once the daily token allowance is used up and tell the user why.
cases.rationale: Enforcing a budget is adk-operational-guardrails; observability only accounts for cost.

cases.prompt: Our coordinator keeps sending billing questions to the tech-support sub-agent. Rewrite the sub-agents' descriptions so routing picks the right one.
cases.rationale: Sub-agent descriptions are instruction text owned by adk-agent-instructions; the orchestration structure is fine.

cases.prompt: The delegated Google Drive OAuth access token shows up in the ADK events our UI receives. Keep it in the credential store and out of state and events.
cases.rationale: Credential custody at the tool boundary is adk-tool-auth-and-secrets.

cases.prompt: Users sometimes paste API keys and card numbers into our ADK chat. Detect and mask them before the model, the session history and the logs see them.
cases.rationale: Screening content for PII and pasted secrets is protect-adk-sensitive-data.

cases.prompt: Roll the new revision of our already-deployed ADK agent out to 10% of traffic, compare eval scores and error rates, and roll back if they regress.
cases.rationale: Canary and rollback of a later release are adk-release-engineering.

cases.prompt: Our client's counsel asked for an AI impact assessment and a system card for the claims agent before the production decision.
cases.rationale: Governance papers for reviewers are adk-governance-pack, not decision material.
